en: Venus spins backwards compared to most other planets, so the sun rises in the west and sets in the east.
Pumice is a volcanic rock so full of trapped gas bubbles that it is the only rock that floats on water.
The moon experiences moonquakes caused by the gravitational pull of Earth, which slightly stretches and squeezes the moon's solid interior.
A single bolt of lightning can heat the surrounding air to 30,000 degrees Celsius, making it five times hotter than the sun's surface.
A single square meter of healthy forest soil can contain over 1,000 earthworms that constantly eat and aerate the dirt.
Groundwater hidden beneath our feet contains more fresh water than all the world's rivers and lakes combined.
A neutron star is so incredibly dense that just one teaspoon of its material would weigh about six billion tons on Earth.
In the deep ocean, a tsunami wave can travel as fast as a jet plane, reaching speeds over 800 kilometers per hour.
The Philippines sits on the Pacific Ring of Fire, a horseshoe-shaped zone responsible for about 90 percent of the world's earthquakes.
Diamonds and pencils share the exact same chemical ingredient, carbon, but their atoms are arranged differently to create extreme hardness.
Jupiter's Great Red Spot is a giant storm that has been raging for over 300 years and is wider than Earth.
A typical fluffy cumulus cloud looks light, but it actually weighs about 500,000 kilograms, which is equal to 100 elephants.
